title: Contradiction Classifier: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Contradiction Classifier does and why archives need it. A contradiction classifier looks at two claims that seem to disagree and decides what kind of disagreement it really is: a direct contradiction, or just different dates, different definitions, different places, or different measurements. Most 'contradictions' turn out to be talking past each other — the classifier proves which ones are real.
demo:
# Contradiction Classifier - runnable demo (JAH-ATK194-000001)
import re
RANK = 1
SIG = False
PAIRS = [('The bridge opened in 1937.', 'The bridge opened in 1939.'), ('The city has 500,000 residents.', 'The city does not have 500,000 residents.'), ('The track is 5 km long.', 'The track is 3.1 mi long.')]  # (claim_a, claim_b)
def classify(a, b):
    la, lb = a.lower(), b.lower()
    da = set(re.findall(r"\b(19|20)\d{2}\b", la)); db = set(re.findall(r"\b(19|20)\d{2}\b", lb))
    if da and db and da != db: return "temporal difference"
    ua = set(re.findall(r"[\d.]+\s*(km|mi|m|kg|lb)", la)); ub = set(re.findall(r"[\d.]+\s*(km|mi|m|kg|lb)", lb))
    if ua and ub and ua != ub: return "measurement difference"
    if ("not " in la) != ("not " in lb): return "direct contradiction"
    nums_a = set(re.findall(r"\b\d[\d,]*\b", la)); nums_b = set(re.findall(r"\b\d[\d,]*\b", lb))
    if nums_a and nums_b and nums_a != nums_b: return "direct contradiction"
    return "scope/wording difference"
for a, b in PAIRS:
    print("[%-26s]" % classify(a, b))
    print("   A: %s\n   B: %s" % (a[:60], b[:60]))
if RANK >= 3:
    from collections import Counter
    print("type histogram:", dict(Counter(classify(a, b) for a, b in PAIRS)))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-CON-" + "JAH-ATK194-000001")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK194-000001", "OK")

title: How the Contradiction Classifier works
description: Overview: what the Contradiction Classifier does and why archives need it. Real classifiers first detect disagreement (negation, antonyms, numeric mismatch), then classify its type: direct contradiction (same subject, predicate, time — opposite values), temporal difference (true at different times), definitional difference ('unemployed' defined differently), scope difference (city vs country), or measurement difference (different units or methods). Each classification cites the reconciling evidence — the differing date, definition, or scope — and only unreconciled oppositions are escalated as genuine contradictions.

t: How the Contradiction Classifier works: the deep tour
title: How the Contradiction Classifier works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Contradiction Classifier does and why archives need it. Real classifiers first detect disagreement (negation, antonyms, numeric mismatch), then classify its type: direct contradiction (same subject, predicate, time — opposite values), temporal difference (true at different times), definitional difference ('unemployed' defined differently), scope difference (city vs country), or measurement difference (different units or methods). Each classification cites the reconciling evidence — the differing date, definition, or scope — and only unreconciled oppositions are escalated as genuine contradictions. Advanced systems use NLI (natural language inference) models for contradiction detection, consult the temporal resolver for date reconciliation and the terminology resolver for definition reconciliation, and track contradiction lifecycles (a dispute later resolved by new evidence). Quality is measured by type-classification accuracy on annotated disagreement corpora. The limits are deep domain disputes where both sides' evidence is real — the classifier reports the dispute with both evidence sets rather than picking a winner.

Each classification cites the reconciling evidence — the differing date, definition, or scope — and only unreconciled oppositions are escalated as genuine contradictions. Advanced systems use NLI (natural language inference) models for contradiction detection, consult the temporal resolver for date reconciliation and the terminology resolver for definition reconciliation, and track contradiction lifecycles (a dispute later resolved by new evidence). Quality is measured by type-classification accuracy on annotated disagreement corpora. The limits are deep domain disputes where both sides' evidence is real — the classifier reports the dispute with both evidence sets rather than picking a winner.

# Contradiction Classifier - runnable demo (JAH-ATK194-000012)
import re
RANK = 3
SIG = False
PAIRS = [('The dam was completed in 1975.', 'The dam was completed in 1975. Still operating.')]  # (claim_a, claim_b)
def classify(a, b):
    la, lb = a.lower(), b.lower()
    da = set(re.findall(r"\b(19|20)\d{2}\b", la)); db = set(re.findall(r"\b(19|20)\d{2}\b", lb))
    if da and db and da != db: return "temporal difference"
    ua = set(re.findall(r"[\d.]+\s*(km|mi|m|kg|lb)", la)); ub = set(re.findall(r"[\d.]+\s*(km|mi|m|kg|lb)", lb))
    if ua and ub and ua != ub: return "measurement difference"
    if ("not " in la) != ("not " in lb): return "direct contradiction"
    nums_a = set(re.findall(r"\b\d[\d,]*\b", la)); nums_b = set(re.findall(r"\b\d[\d,]*\b", lb))
    if nums_a and nums_b and nums_a != nums_b: return "direct contradiction"
    return "scope/wording difference"
for a, b in PAIRS:
    print("[%-26s]" % classify(a, b))
    print("   A: %s\n   B: %s" % (a[:60], b[:60]))
if RANK >= 3:
    from collections import Counter
    print("type histogram:", dict(Counter(classify(a, b) for a, b in PAIRS)))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-CON-" + "JAH-ATK194-000012")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK194-000012", "OK")

title: Using the Contradiction Classifier every day
description: Production: how the Contradiction Classifier runs at archive scale and plugs into the extraction pipeline. A contradiction classifier looks at two claims that seem to disagree and decides what kind of disagreement it really is: a direct contradiction, or just different dates, different definitions, different places, or different measurements. Most 'contradictions' turn out to be talking past each other — the classifier proves which ones are real.
